topic.source_contract: peat extent, depth, condition, hydrology, carbon, ownership, permissions, restoration design, funding, implementation and long-term monitoring evidence

scope_guards: A national peat map is not treated as verified site peat depth.
Mapped deep peat is not treated as current peat condition.
A restoration opportunity is not treated as landowner agreement.
A grant application is not treated as awarded funding.
An awarded grant is not treated as completed restoration.
Drain blocking is not treated as recovered hydrology without monitoring.
Vegetation change is not treated as verified carbon benefit.
No score or promotion is written without exact peat survey, hydrology, rights, funding, implementation and monitored outcomes.
row_checks: Current national and local peat datasets required
Exact peat and project boundary required
Blanket bog, raised bog, fen or lowland peat required
Erosion, vegetation and bare peat condition required
Water table, drains and flow pathways required
Dissolved carbon, sediment and acidity required
SSSI, SAC, SPA and local designations required
Protection, rewetting or revegetation objective required
Drain blocking, reprofiling and vegetation methods required
Construction access and damage controls required
Planning, environmental and protected-site approvals required
Confirmed grant and match funding required
Water table, vegetation, erosion and carbon indicators required
Map, policy or strategy alone is not exact-site delivery
Application or proposal is not approval
Funding announcement is not completed delivery
Current operational use or service required
